// install

From zero to a first run.

Jet is pre-release. Today the supported install path is Nix on x86_64 Linux and macOS; everything else means building from source.

Install with Nix

$ nix --extra-experimental-features "nix-command flakes" \ profile install github:jet-language/jet $ jet version

Install Nix first from nixos.org, then run the command above.

Or build from source

$ git clone https://github.com/jet-language/jet $ cd jet $ nix build $ export PATH="$PWD/result/bin:$PATH" $ jet version

Your first program

$ jet new hello $ cd hello $ jet run hello, world

jet new writes a small project: run.jet with a passing #Test block, a package.jet manifest, and typed command entries. jet run compiles and runs it with the fast profile; jet run --release uses the optimized native build.

When something breaks

Every Jet error has a registered code, a what, a why, and a fix. jet explain takes any code you see and gives the full story offline; jet fix applies the compiler's own suggested repairs to your file.

$ jet explain E0112 $ jet fix run.jet

What works today

  • The compiler, checker, test runner, and formatter are available for the repository's example corpus.
  • Native builds expose both the default fast profile and the optimized release profile.
  • A web-target example is part of the current site corpus; broader browser/UI support remains open.
  • jetpack, the environment engine: declared, reproducible project shells.

What remains under development: Windows support, stability guarantees, and some package-workflow corners. The language is changing weekly, and the diagnostics are the most reliable map of what is true right now.
